long_biography.plain_text:
After extensive damage appeared in a custom-built vessel, David Parker asked its manufacturer to inspect and pay for repairs. The builder attributed the problem to a collision without inspecting the craft, rejecting his claim that construction defects were responsible. Parker and Big Bird Holdings challenged that response under state and federal warranty law.

A four-day federal jury trial found breaches of implied and express warranties and wilful conduct, awarding damages and a civil penalty. The Ninth Circuit affirmed the core result in 2017. Parker died on 1 May 2020; his only child, Jonathan David Parker, was later substituted as successor to the judgment.
